rationale: Because IND_RANK is a monotone transform, dropping the positive-part truncation only breaks ties among cash-surplus firms, making this a near-cosmetic re-run of the archived "Cash-Adjusted Maturity Discretion" (and third variant of the same maturity-weighted financing family) rather than a substantively new mechanism.

Restricting the solvency weight to the capped repurchase leg while preserving the full gross-issuance penalty is a legitimate, diagnosis-motivated asymmetry rather than a pure rescaling of the archived solvency-weighted signal, though the expected incremental gain over talpha 3.26 is modest.

The stated mechanism (penalize issuance that coincides with cash depletion, leaving repurchases untouched) contradicts the expression, since MIN(sstk/at, cash-depletion⁺) is strictly positive for the many net repurchasers that have nonzero gross issuance and declining cash — precisely the firms buybacks mechanically deplete — and this cash-depletion family already delivered near-zero alpha in the archive.

Dollar-capping the maturity-migration penalty at gross repurchases is an economically sensible bound on an already-strong archived signal, but it simultaneously changes the gate from net-repurchaser to any-gross-repurchaser without acknowledging that, so it is an incremental refinement whose incremental content is small.

Replacing the archived all-or-nothing organic-book gate with a dollar cap is a coherent, accounting-consistent graduation that preserves partial credit for aggressive repurchasers, though it recombines two already-tested devices (organic book accretion and dollar capping) rather than introducing a new mechanism.

Relocating the net-liquidity conditioner from the financing leg to the valuation leg is a genuinely distinguishable design that discriminates between the "distress value trap" and "financing discretion" interpretations of the archive's best result, and the sign logic is consistent (nonnegative rank shrinks, never flips, the value score).
